note: The test creates an attribute node through the element API, producing a DOMAttr wrapper backed by libxml state.
The owning element is removed, making the attribute wrapper's backing node potentially detached or invalidated.
The wrapper is accessed after its owner has been removed, exercising stale-node bookkeeping in the DOM extension.
When a DOMAttr wrapper is reinitialized, the constructor reads the previous node pointer from wrapper state before replacement.
The previous node is freed here; the vulnerability hypothesis is that a detached or stale attribute wrapper can make this free unsafe.
The wrapper is updated after the free, so the free is the memory-safety sink in this path.
